input.name: toRoman
input.task: Convert an integer n from 1 to 3999 to a Roman numeral in standard subtractive form (4 is IV, 9 is IX, 40 is XL).

input.name: isPalindrome
input.task: Return true when s reads the same forwards and backwards after you remove every character that is not a letter or a digit and ignore case. An empty string is a palindrome.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

input.name: flatten
input.task: Flatten an array that can hold numbers and arrays nested to any depth into one flat array of numbers, in order. Do not use Array.prototype.flat.

input.name: wordCount
input.task: Count words in text. A word is a run of the letters a to z, compared without case; every other character separates words. Return an object that maps each lowercase word to its count. Empty text gives an empty object.

input.name: mergeIntervals
input.task: Given an array of [start, end] pairs in any order, merge every pair that overlaps or touches (end equal to the next start) and return the merged pairs sorted by start.

input.name: parseDuration
input.task: Parse a duration such as "1h30m", "45s" or "1h2m3s" into a total number of seconds. Units are h, m and s; each appears at most once, in that order, and any of them can be missing.

input.name: lcsLength
input.task: Return the length of the longest common subsequence of strings a and b (characters in the same order, not necessarily next to each other).

input.name: primesUpTo
input.task: Return every prime number less than or equal to n, in increasing order. For n below 2, return an empty array.

input.name: semverCompare
input.task: Compare two semantic version strings of the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optionally followed by -PRERELEASE and/or +BUILD, such as "1.2.3-beta.2+build5". Return -1 if a has lower precedence than b, 1 if it has higher precedence, and 0 if they have equal precedence. Compare MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH as numbers. A version with a prerelease part has lower precedence than the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without one. Compare prerelease parts by their dot-separated identifiers from left to right: two identifiers made only of digits compare as numbers; any other two identifiers compare as strings in plain code-unit order (so uppercase letters sort before lowercase letters); an identifier made only of digits is lower than any other identifier; if all shared identifiers are equal, the version with more identifiers is higher. Ignore build metadata (everything after "+"). Every input is valid.

input.name: runLengthDecode
input.task: Decode run-length text. The input is a sequence of groups, each made of a count and one character: the count is one or more decimal digits and is at least 1 with no leading zero, and the character is any single character that is not a digit. Return the decoded string, where each character is repeated by its count ("3a2b" gives "aaabb", "10x" gives ten x characters). The empty string decodes to the empty string. Return null if the input is not valid: a character with no count in front of it, a count with no character after it, a count of 0, or a count with a leading zero.

input.name: sortRecords
input.task: Sort an array of plain objects by several fields. keys is an array of field names in priority order; a name that starts with "-" means descending order on the field after the dash, any other name means ascending order. Values of one field are numbers or strings: numbers compare numerically and strings compare in plain code-unit order (use < and >, not localeCompare, so "B" sorts before "a"). A record whose value for a field is missing, null or undefined sorts after every record that has a value, in both ascending and descending order; two records that both lack the value tie on that field and the next key decides. Records that tie on every key keep their original relative order. Return a new array and do not change the input.

input.name: humanizeDuration
input.task: Turn a number of seconds into text with the units d (86400 seconds), h (3600), m (60) and s, largest first, each written as the number followed by the unit letter, separated by single spaces. Leave out every unit whose value is 0: 3725 gives "1h 2m 5s" and 90000 gives "1d 1h". Zero seconds gives "0s". Do not carry hours into days beyond what the units above give (there are no weeks or months). If the input is not a number, is negative, or is not a whole number, return null.

input.name: freeSlots
input.task: busy is an array of [from, to] pairs of numbers (from is less than to) in any order. They may overlap, touch, or lie partly or completely outside the window. Return the free time inside the window from start to end as a sorted array of [from, to] pairs: the parts of the window that are not covered by any busy pair. Do not return empty pairs (from equal to to). A busy pair that only touches the window at one point covers nothing. If the window is empty (end is not greater than start), return an empty array.

input.name: parseQuery
input.task: Parse a URL query string into an object. Remove one leading "?" if there is one. Split the rest on "&" and skip empty parts. Split each part at its first "=" into a key and a value; a part with no "=" has the value "" (empty string). Decode keys and values: "+" becomes a space, and percent escapes such as %E2%82%AC are decoded as UTF-8 (decodeURIComponent does this); if a piece has a malformed escape, keep that piece as it is, only with "+" turned into a space. Skip a part whose decoded key is empty. A key that occurs once maps to its value as a string; a key that occurs more than once maps to an array of all its values in order of appearance.

input.name: wrapText
input.task: Word-wrap text greedily into lines of at most width characters (width is at least 1). Words are separated by runs of whitespace; ignore leading and trailing whitespace and write exactly one space between words on a line. Put each word on the current line if it fits (line length, one space, word length is at most width), else start a new line with it. A word longer than width is cut into chunks of width characters: it first ends the current line, every chunk except the last is a line of its own, and the last chunk (1 to width characters) becomes the current line, which later words may join. Return the lines as an array. Text with no words gives an empty array.

input.name: topoOrder
input.task: deps is an object that maps a task name to an array of the task names that must run before it. A task that only appears inside an array (not as a key) is also a task, with no prerequisites. The same prerequisite may be listed twice. Return all tasks in an order where every task comes after all its prerequisites. When several tasks are ready at the same time, always pick the one that comes first in plain code-unit order of the names (so "B" comes before "a"). Return null if the tasks cannot all be ordered because of a cycle; a task that lists itself is a cycle. An empty object gives an empty array.

input.name: cidrContains
input.task: cidr is text such as "192.168.1.0/24" (an IPv4 address, a slash, and a prefix length) and ip is an IPv4 address. Return true when ip lies inside the range that cidr describes. Only the first prefix-length bits of the cidr address matter, so "192.168.1.77/24" describes the same range as "192.168.1.0/24"; a prefix of 0 matches every address. An IPv4 address is exactly four decimal parts separated by dots, each from 0 to 255, with no leading zeros ("0" is fine, "01" is not), no spaces and no other characters. The prefix length is a whole number from 0 to 32 written the same way (no leading zeros). If cidr or ip is not valid, return false.

input.name: compactRanges
input.task: nums is an array of integers in any order, possibly with duplicates. Sort them, drop duplicates, and find the maximal runs of consecutive integers (each one more than the one before). Write a run of three or more as "first-last". Write a run of one or two numbers as the plain numbers. Join all parts with "," and no spaces. Negative numbers keep their minus sign, so the run -3, -2, -1 is "-3--1". An empty array gives the empty string.

input.name: expandBraces
input.task: Expand shell-style brace groups. A group is "{", alternatives separated by commas, and "}"; an alternative may be empty and may contain further groups. Return every expansion as an array. The order is that of reading left to right: for the string "{a,b}{c,d}" the result is ["ac","ad","bc","bd"] (the first group changes slowest, and the alternatives of a group are used in the order written). Text with no braces gives an array with that text alone. A group with one alternative and no comma, like "{x}", is still a group, so "a{x}b" gives ["axb"]. Keep duplicates. The input always has balanced braces.

input.name: businessDays
input.task: start and end are valid calendar dates written "YYYY-MM-DD" in the Gregorian calendar. Count the days d with start <= d < end (the end day is not counted) that fall on Monday to Friday. There are no holidays. If end is not after start, return 0. Do not depend on the machine's time zone.
